Check a user-defined count family

Source: R/user_families.R
check_count_family.Rd

Runs numerical checks of a family made with new_count_family() over a grid of means and parameter values: that the probabilities sum to one, that the mean is \(\mu\) (when mean_is_mu = TRUE) or matches the mean function, that the variance, cdf and rand functions (when given) agree with the PMF, that inputs are recycled, and that missing and invalid values give -Inf rather than errors.

Usage

check_count_family(
  family,
  mu = c(0.05, 1, 20),
  par = list(),
  tol = 1e-06,
  nsim = 2000
)

Arguments

family

a family from new_count_family().

mu

means to check.

par

a named list with values of each parameter (on the parameter's own scale); every combination with mu is checked.

tol

tolerance for the comparisons.

nsim

draws per grid point to check rand (0 to skip).

Value

A data frame with one row per check (check, ok, detail), printed, and returned invisibly. A warning lists the checks that failed.

Examples

nb_theta <- new_count_family(
  name = "NB-theta",
  params = list(theta = count_param("log")),
  logpmf = function(y, mu, par)
    dnbinom(y, size = par$theta, mu = mu, log = TRUE),
  variance = function(mu, par) mu + mu^2 / par$theta)
check_count_family(nb_theta, mu = c(0.1, 2, 30),
                   par = list(theta = c(0.5, 5)))
#>                        check   ok                                    detail
#>                PMF sums to 1 TRUE               largest |sum - 1| = 1.1e-16
#>               mean equals mu TRUE          largest relative error = 5.2e-11
#>   variance() matches the PMF TRUE          largest relative error = 1.3e-09
#>            vectorized over y TRUE                                        ok
#>              NA mean handled TRUE                                  no error
#>  invalid mean gives no error TRUE no error (the row is given probability 0)
